topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and states what students should learn.

topics.label: The genetic and cellular basis of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations can give cells an evolutionary advantage that leads to cancer under permissive conditions.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risk, chance and epidemiological evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental exposures to cancer risk and why cancer cannot simply be attributed to bad luck.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer causation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can contribute to cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example.

topics.label: How environmental mutagens damage DNA
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage that can become mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show why initiating mutations may require a growth-promoting environment before tumours develop.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how carcinogenic effects depend on the exposed tissue's biological context and consolidate the preceding mechanisms of carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Identifying carcinogenic exposures in human populations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence from people can connect particular exposures with cancer development.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate how experimental tests detect carcinogenic potential and why their results do not fully predict cancer risk in humans.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and placing cancer risks within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
